responsibility: This module is GCC’s architecture-independent target-common configuration layer for machine ports: it collects the per-target files that plug each backend into shared option handling before the main target-specific code-generation logic runs. Across subdirectories named for architectures, the recurring *-common.c and *-common.cc files define targetm_common hooks, baseline target flag sets, optimization-default tables, exception and unwind policy, and early validation or normalization of target switches such as -march, -mcpu, -mtune, ABI, FPU, TLS, endianness, and small-data options. For richer ports such as AArch64, ARM, x86, RISC-V, RS/6000, and S/390, this layer also owns canonical CPU/ISA name registries, extension parsing, feature tables, multilib or assembler-facing option rewriting, and runtime CPU-feature metadata headers like cpuinfo.h and ISA definition tables; for simpler ports it often just instantiates default common hooks. In short, gcc/common/config is the shared front end of GCC’s target backends, responsible for turning command-line machine selections and target-wide policy into normalized internal option state that later backend, lowering, and emission stages consume.
